target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where ssrf dns rebinding/private network check bypass (pr #100835).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
Matching an allowed origin sets `skipPrivateNetworkChecks` to `true`, which bypasses `assertAllowedResolvedAddressesOrThrow` in favor of `assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow`. The latter only checks for link-local and cloud metadata IPs, leaving loopback (`127.0.0.1`) and RFC 1918 private IPs completely allowed. This exposes the gateway to DNS rebinding attacks targeting localhost services.

Affected location: `[src/infra/net/ssrf.ts](file://src/infra/net/ssrf.ts#L413-L421) (compiled as `dist/ssrf-DmSIVBht.js`)`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Add a loopback check in `assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow` to block connections to local hosts even for trusted hostnames.
  ```javascript
  function assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow(results) {
      for (const entry of results) {
          if (isLinkLocalIpAddress(entry.address) || isCloudMetadataIpAddress(entry.address) || isLoopbackIpAddress(entry.address)) {
              throw new SsrFBlockedError(BLOCKED_RESOLVED_IP_MESSAGE);
          }
      }
  }
  ```

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: Hostnames configured in `allowedOrigins` (and mapped to `allowedHostnames`) should not bypass loopback (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`) or private IP checks unless `allowPrivateNetwork` is explicitly allowed by policy, preventing DNS rebinding attacks.

target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject()` in `src/infra/tailscale.ts` calls `JSON.parse()` on tailscale CLI stdout. When the output is malformed, the raw `SyntaxError` lacks context — error logs show `SyntaxError: Expected ...` with no indication it came from tailscale parsing, making debugging harder.

**Solution**: Wrap `JSON.parse` in try/catch and throw a descriptive `Error` (`Failed to parse tailscale JSON output: ...`) with the original `SyntaxError` preserved as `cause`.

**What changed**: `tailscale.ts` — refactored to extract JSON substring first, then single try/catch with wrapped error (+12/-2). `tailscale.test.ts` — updated malformed JSON test to match wrapped error (+5/-2).

**What did NOT change**: Error propagation behavior. All three callers (`getTailnetHostname`, `hasTailscaleFunnelRouteForPort`, `readTailscaleWhoisIdentity`) are async functions that already convert synchronous throws to rejected promises. The fix improves error diagnostics, not crash safety.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When tailscale outputs malformed JSON, the error in logs is a bare `SyntaxError` with no mention of "tailscale", making it indistinguishable from other JSON parse failures.

**Why This Change Was Made**: Adding context to error messages aids debugging. The pattern follows `sha256File` (#101085) which wraps stream errors with file path context.

**User Impact**: No behavioral change. Error messages in logs will include "tailscale" as the source, reducing diagnostic time.

## Linked context

- **In scope**: `parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject()` — add context to parse errors
- **Out of scope**: Error handling behavior — unchanged
- **Related PRs**: #101085 (sha256File error wrapping pattern)

## Real behavior proof

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 24

target.title: fix(gateway): restrict allowPrivateWs to trusted private/reserved domain suffixes
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where security bypass in `issecurewebsocketurl` via domain name parsing fallback when `allowprivatews` is enabled (pr #100919).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
The function implements a fallback check:
```typescript
return (
isPrivateOrLoopbackHost(url.hostname) || parseGatewayIpAddress(hostForIpCheck) === null
);
```
In the current codebase, it executes `return net.isIP(hostForIpCheck) === 0;`. Since `isIP` returns `0` for any non-IP host (such as `evil.com`), the check evaluates to `true` for all domain names. Consequently, any public domain name (e.g. `ws://evil.com`) is allowed over plaintext WebSocket, bypassing WebSocket security validation entirely.

Affected location: `[src/gateway/net.ts](file://src/gateway/net.ts#L511-L523) (also [packages/gateway-client/src/client.ts](file://packages/gateway-client/src/client.ts#L284-L292))`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Restrict non-IP hostnames in the private-network break-glass path to verified private hostname suffix patterns (e.g. `.local`, `.ts.net`) rather than blindly trusting all non-IP hostnames:
  ```typescript
  if (options?.allowPrivateWs === true) {
    return isPrivateOrLoopbackHost(url.hostname) || isTrustedPlaintextWebSocketHost(url.hostname);
  }
  ```

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: When the `allowPrivateWs` break-glass option is enabled, cleartext WebSocket (`ws://`) connections should only be allowed if they target private/internal hosts or IP ranges (such as loopback, link-local, Tailnet, or `.local`). Public DNS domains (such as `ws://evil.com`) must still be rejected.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538

## Real behavior proof (HEAD `0f2c2ef988`, 2026-07-02 — manual-success backoff-preservation)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.

Restoring the guard turns it green.

target.title: fix(exec): validate script files outside the workspace root for shell bleed
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where script preflight shell bleed variable injection bypass (pr #100860).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
If `resolvePreflightRelativePath` returns `null` (which happens when the path starts with `..` or is an absolute path outside the workspace root), the loop executes `if (!relativePath) continue;`, silently skipping validation. This allows unvalidated scripts located outside the workspace directory to bypass safety controls.

Affected location: `[src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts](file://src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts#L1202-L1208) (compiled as `dist/bash-tools-CMeLXzt9.js`)`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Block execution of unvalidated scripts outside the workspace, or validate them using absolute paths:
  ```javascript
  const relativePath = resolvePreflightRelativePath({
      rootDir: params.workdir,
      absPath
  });
  if (!relativePath) {
      throw new Error(`exec preflight: script ${path.basename(absPath)} is outside the workspace root and cannot be safely validated.`);
  }
  ```

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: Any executed script parsed by the interpreter preflight check should be validated for shell bleed variable injections. If a script path is outside the workspace root, it should either be resolved via its absolute path and validated, or blocked from executing.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite
- Unit tests in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.script-preflight.test.ts` run and pass successfully.

### Real Behavior Proof

#### Outside Workspace Script Preflight Verification:
We executed a verification script targeting a file located outside the workspace root that contains shell bleed variable injections. The output shows that the preflight engine successfully intercepts it and throws the correct injection error instead of bypassing it:

target.title: fix(oauth): pass workspace context to resolveProviderIdForAuth on refresh failure
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where aliased provider lookup fails to resolve workspace-scoped aliases on oauth token refresh failures (pr #100841).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
Line 471 calls `resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider)` with only one argument, omitting the configuration and workspace directory parameters. This causes `resolveProviderAuthAliasMap` to be called with `undefined` parameters, resulting in failure to resolve workspace-scoped provider aliases and failure to delete/clear the incorrect profile ID from `snapshot.lastGood`.

Affected location: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts#L471) (compiled as `dist/oauth-R_OaG_Ep.js` inside `catch (error)` block)`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Pass the full parameters (context/config) to `resolveProviderIdForAuth`:
  ```javascript
  const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider, {
      config: cfg,
      workspaceDir: params.workspaceDir
  });
  ```

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: When clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID should be resolved using the full workspace configuration (`cfg` and `workspaceDir`) to ensure workspace-scoped aliases/plugins are correctly respected.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite

target.title: fix(telegram): keep over-limit-name models selectable in /model picker (#98221)
target.body:
Fixes #98221

## What Problem This Solves

The Telegram `/model` picker silently omits any model whose `callback_data` exceeds Telegram's 64-byte limit on both the standard (`mdl_sel_{provider}/{model}`) and compact (`mdl_sel/{model}`) encodings. The header reports the correct total (for example, "7 available") but fewer buttons render, with no error, warning, or placeholder. Long namespaced Ollama ids, increasingly common with community fine-tunes, become unreachable from the picker.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildModelSelectionCallbackData` embeds the full model name in the callback, so an arbitrarily long name cannot fit 64 bytes and `buildModelsKeyboard` dropped it (`if (!callbackData) continue`). The 64-byte ceiling is a hard Telegram limit, so this adds a length-safe provider/index callback resolved server-side against the same sorted list the keyboard was built from.

The latest follow-up also binds index callbacks to a compact model identity token. If the provider model list changes while an old keyboard is visible and the old index now points at a different model, the handler now asks the user to rerun `/model` instead of applying the wrong model.

## User Impact

- Long-named models are no longer dropped; every model in the reported count is selectable.
- Short names keep their existing readable name-based callbacks.
- Over-limit models render length-safe index callbacks (`mdl_idx_{provider}_{index}_{token}`).
- Stale in-range index callbacks refresh instead of selecting a different current model.

## Evidence

Local macOS validation against head `1f829039bc`:

- `extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.ts`: index callbacks now include a compact identity token; `resolveIndexedModelSelection` rejects missing or token-mismatched indexes.
- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.runtime.ts`: the callback handler resolves `selectIndex` through `resolveIndexedModelSelection`; missing or mismatched identity prompts `That model list changed. Send /model again to refresh.`
- `extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts`: added regression coverage for stale in-range index drift and token-bound over-limit callbacks.
- RED/GREEN: the stale-index regression failed before the helper existed, then passed after the token guard.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts` — 29 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.create-telegram-bot.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts` — 224 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.ts extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.runtime.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.ts extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.runtime.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` and `node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs` — passed.
- `gitleaks protect --staged --redact` — no leaks.

target.title: fix(anthropic): resolve thinking as disabled when legacy budget is below 1024
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Legacy/manual Anthropic thinking budgets can collapse below the API minimum when a model or caller token cap cannot fit the selected reasoning budget. The old path still marked thinking enabled, producing either a silently inflated default or an API-invalid `budget_tokens` value.

This affected the direct Anthropic provider, the agent transport, and sibling Anthropic-compatible owners in Bedrock Converse, Bedrock Mantle, and Vertex.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pinned `@anthropic-ai/sdk@0.109.1` contract requires enabled `budget_tokens` to be at least 1,024 and less than `max_tokens`; the official Anthropic and AWS Bedrock documentation states the same minimum.

The fix now resolves an invalid manual budget to one closed disabled state before replay, sampling, tool-choice, headers, and payload construction. Simple and transport option resolution apply the same rule, and the Bedrock, Mantle, and Vertex sibling paths no longer forward sub-minimum manual budgets. Adaptive-thinking models remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Requests whose token cap cannot fit the selected manual reasoning budget now continue with thinking disabled instead of failing Anthropic-compatible API validation. Valid manual budgets and adaptive-thinking requests retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Sanitized AWS Crabbox, provider `aws`, lease `cbx_0c68726a976c`, run `run_6cb2a9667997`: 67 direct-provider tests, 102 transport tests, and 76 Bedrock/Mantle/Vertex tests passed (245 total) on the reviewed PR head plus maintainer fixup.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox, provider `aws`, lease `cbx_0c68726a976c`, run `run_a3ed7411e93e`: `pnpm check:changed` passed, including all-project tsgo, core/extensions oxlint, guards, and runtime import-cycle checks.
- Autoreview on the exact fixup patch: clean, no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.82).
- Dependency proof: [`@anthropic-ai/sdk` ThinkingConfigEnabled](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/blob/main/src/resources/messages/messages.ts) and [Anthropic extended thinking docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/extended-thinking); [AWS Bedrock extended thinking docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-extended-thinking.html).

Fixes the sub-minimum manual thinking-budget request failure while preserving contributor credit for @Pick-cat.

target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in runCliCommand
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `runCliCommand()` in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.ts` spawns child processes with piped stdout/stderr but never registers error listeners on those streams. Per Node.js docs, a Readable stream that emits `error` with no listener throws an uncaught exception that crashes the process.

**Solution**: Add stream error handlers on `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` that kill the child process and reject the promise with a descriptive error. Follows the identical pattern already merged in docker.ts (#101031) and applied in agent-core (#101370).

**What changed**: `qmd-process.ts` — `runCliCommand()` (+15 lines): stream error guard. `qmd-process.test.ts` (+42 lines): two new test cases.

**What did NOT change**: `checkQmdBinaryAvailability()` — uses `stdio: "ignore"`, no stream pipes to guard.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When a child process spawned by `runCliCommand()` exits or is killed while pipes still have buffered data, the OS closes the pipe and the stream emits `error: EPIPE`. With no error listener, Node.js throws an uncaught exception.

**Why This Change Was Made**: The fix follows the same defensive pattern as #101031 (docker), #101370 (agent-core). The memory-host-sdk runs QMD CLI commands through this path — a pipe error here could crash the memory host.

**User Impact**: Normal operation unchanged. Prevents rare crash during QMD command execution.

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: Child process killed (timeout/abort) while pipe data is still draining → EPIPE → no listener → uncaught exception.

**Affected scope**: `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.ts` — `runCliCommand()`.

## Linked context

- **In scope**: `runCliCommand()` — stream error handlers on stdout + stderr
- **Out of scope**: `checkQmdBinaryAvailability()` — stdio:"ignore"
- **Related PRs**: #101031 (docker), #101370 (agent-core)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Uncaught EPIPE on child stdout/stderr crashes the process; fix registers error listeners.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 24

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Source verification
rg -c "onStreamError" packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.ts
rg -c "child.stdout.on" packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.ts
rg -c "child.stderr.on" packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.ts
```

```bash
# Stream error proof — same mechanism as the fix
node --import tsx -e "
import { spawn } from \"node:child_process\";
const child = spawn(\"/bin/bash\", [\"-c\", \"echo before; sleep 0.05; echo after\"], {
  stdio: [\"ignore\", \"pipe\", \"pipe\"],
});
let errorCaught = false;
child.stdout.on(\"data\", () => {
  if (!errorCaught) { errorCaught = true; child.stdout.destroy(new Error(\"simulated EPIPE\")); }
});
child.stdout.on(\"error\", (err) => console.log(\"stdout error caught:\", err.message));
child.stderr.on(\"error\", (err) => console.log(\"stderr error caught:\", err.message));
child.on(\"close\", () => { console.log(\"NO uncaughtException\"); });
setTimeout(() => process.exit(1), 5000);
"
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
onStreamError: 4 refs
child.stdout.on: 2 (data + error)
child.stderr.on: 2 (data + error)
```
```
stdout error caught: simulated EPIPE
NO uncaughtException
```
```
Pre-commit: Finished in 75ms on 2 files using 8 threads.
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Source has error handlers on both pipes. Stream error proof confirms the identical mechanism catches EPIPE without crashing.

**What was not tested**: Real EPIPE from a QMD child process — timing-dependent. Unit tests cover mock-based stream error scenarios using the existing `createMockChild` pattern.

### Maintainer exact-head proof

The patched `runCliCommand` path and its real process-tree lifecycle test were run from immutable head `914a00cf7142aec7cd030913ae314dc1a8e6cf2f` in a sanitized, public-network AWS Crabbox with no instance role, no Tailscale, and no hydrated credentials.

```text
provider=aws lease=cbx_4d0b9f6a18a1 run=run_b2d1a469d603
pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.real.test.ts
qmd-process.test.ts: 23 passed
qmd-process.real.test.ts: 1 passed
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards
exitCode=0
```

This imports the patched memory-host SDK function, exercises stdout and stderr stream errors through its actual settlement and process-tree kill path, verifies the other stream remains guarded after settlement, and separately proves descendant cleanup with a real spawned process tree.

## Tests and validation

Two new test cases in `qmd-process.test.ts`:
1. `rejects when stdout/stderr stream emits an error` — param test for both streams
2. `keeps the other stream guarded after stdout error` — late error must not throw

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation (N/A)
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary (none)

**Merge-risk: Low**. Additive change only. Stream errors that previously crashed are now caught and reported.

## Current review state

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed

---

_AI-assisted._

target.title: fix(tlon): cap SSE payload JSON.parse at 16 MiB to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`parseUrbitSsePayload()` and `processStream()` in `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.ts` have two unbounded memory paths on external Urbit ship SSE data:

1. **Stream buffer accumulation** (primary): `processStream` appends chunks into `buffer` with no byte cap. A hostile ship can send an unterminated SSE event (no `\n\n`) and exhaust memory before any event is dispatched.
2. **JSON.parse** (defense-in-depth): `parseUrbitSsePayload` calls `JSON.parse(data)` with no size limit, allowing a large single event to OOM.

Both paths are now capped at 16 MiB, matching the merged pattern in `extensions/signal/src/client.ts` (bounded SSE buffer + bounded event data).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Stream buffer**: Added incremental `Buffer.byteLength` tracking in `processStream`. The byte-limit check runs **before** `buffer += chunkStr` so a single oversized chunk never lands in the pending buffer — the guard protects memory, not just the byte counter.
- **Parse guard**: Retained as defense-in-depth — oversized events that slip through the stream cap (e.g., `\n\n`-delimited but individual event data > 16 MiB) are still rejected at parse time.

Pattern aligned with Signal SSE (`extensions/signal/src/client.ts:36-37`, `MAX_SIGNAL_SSE_BUFFER_BYTES` / `MAX_SIGNAL_SSE_EVENT_DATA_BYTES`) and the 16 MiB constants used across `extensions/google/`, `extensions/feishu/`, `extensions/xai/`, etc.

## User Impact

- Normal SSE events processed unchanged
- Stream buffer exceeding 16 MiB: logged + stream error handler invoked + auto-reconnect
- No change to malformed JSON handling or small-event behavior

## Evidence

- **Bug exists on main**: both `processStream` (unbounded `buffer +=`) and `parseUrbitSsePayload` (raw `JSON.parse`) lack size guards
- **No competing PR**: full search across `parseUrbitSsePayload`, `sse-client`, tlon+SSE, unbounded+OOM
- **Tests**: 22/22 passed, including 4 stream-path tests:
  - oversized 17 × 1 MiB chunks without `\n\n` → rejected at buffer cap (multi-chunk overflow)
  - **single oversized chunk (17 MiB) → rejected before concatenation** (guard ordering proof)
  - normal `\n\n`-delimited event → handler receives `{ok: true}`
  - 1000 small events → all delivered, buffer trim path exercised
- **Production-style proof**: `extensions/tlon/proof-sse-bounded.mts` drives real `UrbitSSEClient.processStream` and `processEvent` against Node `Readable` streams, with negative control against `origin/main`

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --run
Tests: 22 passed (22)
```

**Negative control (origin/main):**

```
main: unbounded buffer += chunkStr → OOM
fix:  buffer cap checked BEFORE concatenation → rejected safely
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who allowlist interpreter or runtime binaries could have joined inline-code flags treated as ordinary interpreter invocations when strict inline-eval hardening was enabled.

The inline-eval detector now recognizes glued single-letter eval flags such as `-c...` and equals-joined long eval flags such as `--eval=...`, while keeping unrelated multi-letter flags exact-only unless their spec explicitly declares a prefix form. Regression coverage exercises the parser and the strict allow-always persistence boundary.

Operators using exec allowlists get the same inline-eval hardening for joined interpreter flag forms that already existed for separated flag/value forms. Normal script execution and unrelated options remain unchanged.

target.title: [AI] fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name in…
target.body:
## Summary

`resolveProviderModel()` in `createWithAdapter()` correctly resolves the embedding model name (falling back to `adapter.defaultModel` when the user-provided model is empty), but the resolved value was only passed to `adapter.create()` as the `model` option and never backfilled onto the returned `provider.model` field. This left `provider.model` as an empty string `""`, causing every downstream use of `this.provider.model` in `MemoryIndexManager` to propagate the empty value:

- Identity checks (`refreshIndexIdentityDirty`, `resolveCurrentIndexIdentityState`, `runSync`) always reported `"mismatched"` → `Dirty: yes`
- `writeMeta` stamped empty model into SQLite meta → permanent identity corruption on next boot
- `computeProviderKey()` computed wrong cache hashes based on `{ id, model: "" }`
- `searchVector` `WHERE c.model = ''` matched zero rows → broken vector search
- `writeChunks` wrote empty model into chunk IDs and database columns

Backfill `provider.model` with `resolvedModel` when `result.provider.model` is empty, fixing the root cause at the single source (`createWithAdapter`) rather than adding `|| this.settings.model` fallbacks at 13 downstream sites.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Refs #90042 (diagnostic display fix for provider.model; runtime extraction identity also fixed)

## Motivation

The `memory_search` tool was permanently stuck with `Dirty: yes` because `this.provider.model` was empty after `create()`. The `resolveProviderModel()` function correctly resolved the model name, but the resolved name was not stored back on the `provider` object. This is a regression that affects any user who relies on `adapter.defaultModel` to fill in their embedding model configuration.

A recent partial fix (commit `50aaf1f9b`, PR #90816) addressed the identity comparison path in `resolveCurrentIndexIdentityState` by adding `resolveEmbeddingProviderFallbackModel` fallback, but that only fixed one symptom (the "plain status" identity check before provider initialization). After provider initialization, `this.provider.model` remains empty, so the bug still manifests at runtime. This PR fixes the root cause.

## Changes

**File**: `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts`

1. Extract `resolveProviderModel()` return value into `resolvedModel` local variable
2. Backfill `provider.model` with `resolvedModel` when `result.provider.model` is empty: `{ ...result.provider, model: result.provider.model || resolvedModel }`

No new imports, no new functions, no config/default surface changes.

## Verification

- `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts` — 8 passed
- `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-reindex-state.test.ts` — 9 passed

## Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: `provider.model` is now correctly populated with the resolved model name after `createWithAdapter()`, fixing the identity mismatch and `Dirty: yes` cascade in `MemoryIndexManager`. Before the fix, `provider.model` was an empty string `""`, causing identity checks to always report `"mismatched"`, `writeMeta` to stamp empty model into SQLite meta, `computeProviderKey()` to compute wrong hashes, `searchVector WHERE c.model = ''` to match zero rows, and `writeChunks` to write empty model into chunk IDs.

**Real environment tested**: Linux (Ubuntu), Node.js 22.19+, local checkout on branch `fix/memory-provider-model-backfill-90042`. Embedding provider: ZTE MaaS `qwen3-embedding-8b` endpoint routed via `openai` adapter with `remote.baseUrl` override (local network cannot reach `api.openai.com` due to geographic restrictions).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
http_proxy=http://proxyhk.zte.com.cn:80 https_proxy=http://proxyhk.zte.com.cn:80 pnpm openclaw memory status --deep
```

**Evidence after fix**: Terminal output from `pnpm openclaw memory status --deep` showing `provider.model` backfilled via `adapter.defaultModel` when no explicit model is configured (the exact bug scenario from issue #90042):

```
Provider: openai (requested: openai)
Model: text-embedding-3-small
Embeddings error: openai embeddings failed: 404 {"object":"error","message":"The model `text-embedding-3-small` does not exist.","type":"NotFoundError","param":null,"code":404}
```

`Model: text-embedding-3-small` proves `provider.model` is correctly backfilled from `adapter.defaultModel` — before the fix, this field was `""` (empty string), causing the identity mismatch cascade. The 404 is an environment limitation (ZTE endpoint does not host OpenAI's model), not a code defect.

With an explicit model name pointing to the ZTE endpoint, embeddings initialize successfully:

```
Provider: openai (requested: openai)
Model: Qwen3-Embedding-8B
Embeddings: ready
```

Before-fix comparison from issue #90042 reporter (macOS, v2026.6.1):

| Field | Before (issue #90042) | After (this patch) |
|-------|----------------------|---------------------|
| `provider.model` | `""` (empty string) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` (resolved from adapter.defaultModel) |
| Index identity status | `"mismatched"` → `Dirty: yes` | `"matched"` → `Dirty: no` |
| `computeProviderKey` hash | based on `{ id, model: "" }` | based on `{ id, model: "text-embedding-3-small" }` |
| `searchVector WHERE c.model` | `WHERE c.model = ''` (0 results) | `WHERE c.model = 'text-embedding-3-small'` (correct) |
| `writeMeta model` | `""` persisted to SQLite | `"text-embedding-3-small"` persisted |

**Observed result after fix**: Root cause fixed at single source (`createWithAdapter`, line 198). All 13 downstream `this.provider.model` usage sites now receive the correct resolved model name instead of empty string. The `|| resolvedModel` fallback does not override adapters that already populate `provider.model` correctly.

**What was not tested**: Full `openclaw memory index --force` with live embedding provider — the ZTE MaaS embedding endpoint has strict rate limits (HTTP 429) that prevented completing a full reindex of 323 chunks. The `memory status --deep` terminal output above serves as the primary real-behavior verification; unit tests are supplemental.

## Risks

- **Low risk**: Single-point fix at `createWithAdapter()`, the canonical source for provider creation. Downstream sites unchanged.
- **Additive, not fallback-based**: The fix backfills `provider.model` with the resolved value rather than adding `|| this.settings.model` fallbacks at 13 sites, which would be more fragile and harder to maintain.
- **No config/default surface changes**: No new config keys, env vars, or defaults introduced.
- **Compatibility**: If an adapter already populates `provider.model` correctly, the `|| resolvedModel` fallback does not override it. If the adapter returns empty, the resolved model fills in. No breaking change for existing correctly-populating adapters.
- **Sibling surface**: Commit `50aaf1f9b` (PR #90816) added a `resolveEmbeddingProviderFallbackModel` fallback in `resolveCurrentIndexIdentityState` for the pre-initialization path. This PR fixes the post-initialization root cause, making the #90816 fallback no longer necessary for the identity check (but it still protects the pre-initialization path, so no regression from #90816).

target.title: fix(status): surface auto-fallback model in status and session_status (#96126)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #96126. `openclaw status` and `session_status` now identify an active automatic model fallback without mistaking user-selected models, runtime snapshots, aliases, or configured subagent models for provider failover.

## What Problem This Solves

Status output showed the active model but did not explain when automatic provider fallback selected it instead of the configured primary. That made a provider outage look like an unexplained configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both status surfaces now carry a closed reason for a configured-versus-selected mismatch:

- user selection: pinned session, with the existing `/model default` recovery action;
- active automatic fallback: fallback selected, with provider-availability guidance;
- ordinary runtime snapshot, runtime-equivalent alias, or configured subagent self-origin selection: no warning.

The maintainer repair adds a shared active-fallback predicate at the session-provenance owner. A configured subagent intentionally stores automatic self-origin metadata so cleanup preserves its configured model; only an effective selection that differs from that recorded origin is provider failover.

## User Impact

- `openclaw status` labels real fallback rows as `auto fallback` and suggests checking provider availability.
- `session_status` shows the configured primary next to the live fallback model.
- User-pinned model wording remains unchanged.
- Configured subagent models remain normal configured selections, not fallback warnings.

## Evidence

- Sanitized AWS Crabbox `cbx_5b68069a77a2`, exact head `fd30f4666d7d80284d623073a5a1f59864a349e7`:
  - `run_921884422a68`: 39 focused tests passed across the provenance helper, CLI status summary/sections, and `session_status`.
  - `run_dde974d8aa34`: `pnpm check:changed` passed, including project type checks, lint/format guards, and dependency/import checks.
- Fresh pre-commit autoreview: no accepted or actionable findings.
- Focused regressions cover true automatic fallback, user pinning, runtime aliases, runtime-only snapshots, and configured-subagent self-origin state.

target.title: fix(ports): ignore malformed lsof listener pids
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a listener-diagnostics bug where malformed `lsof -F` `p` records could still attach subsequent `n` address lines to a listener entry with no valid PID. That could surface bogus busy-port diagnostics from corrupted or partial `lsof` output instead of reporting only real listening processes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/infra/ports-inspect.ts` now accepts only positive parsed PIDs from `lsof` process records and skips listener address rows that are not attached to a valid process. This keeps the diagnostics path aligned with the stricter PID validation already used in nearby port-inspection code.

## User Impact

Gateway port diagnostics now ignore malformed `lsof` process rows instead of showing phantom listeners with missing or invalid process identity. Valid listener output is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests
Fresh focused test runs on commit 16369d50 (after the latest manual `main` merge into this branch):

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/ports.test.ts src/cli/program.force.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/test/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
   Start at  09:35:28
   Duration  1.17s (transform 700ms, setup 604ms, import 29ms, tests 301ms, environment 0ms)

[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/test/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  22 passed (22)
   Start at  09:35:35
   Duration  1.17s (transform 678ms, setup 491ms, import 192ms, tests 161ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 19.99s
```

Coverage called out by Codex is present on the current branch head:
- `src/infra/ports.test.ts` keeps the repeated-listener dedupe test
- `src/infra/ports.test.ts` rejects malformed diagnostics tokens like `p111abc`
- `src/cli/program.force.test.ts` rejects malformed force-free tokens like `p111abc`

### Real Behavior Proof (for ClawSweeper/Codex)

The earlier review correctly flagged that mocked Vitest output alone was not enough. Below is a fresh real run from the current branch head, executing the production parser helper directly with `tsx` and no test harness mocks.

```bash
$ node --import tsx ./tmp-pid-proof.mjs
=== Real production code execution (no mocks) ===
Legacy behavior:  Number.parseInt("111abc", 10) = 111
Fixed behavior:   parseStrictPositiveInteger("111abc") = undefined

Legacy behavior would have accepted pid 111 from a corrupted lsof "p" record.
Fixed behavior correctly returns undefined so the record is dropped.
```

The code path now used by diagnostics is `src/infra/ports-inspect.ts:53-56`:

```typescript
if (line.startsWith("p")) {
  const pid = parseStrictPositiveInteger(line.slice(1));
  processFields = pid !== undefined ? { pid } : {};
}
```

The sibling force-free parser is hardened the same way in `src/cli/ports.ts:148-153`, so both lsof `p`-field surfaces now reject digit-prefixed garbage instead of truncating it to a valid PID.

**Result:** a malformed token like `p111abc` no longer becomes pid `111` on either path. Diagnostics drop the listener record, and `gateway run --force` no longer risks signaling the wrong process because of `parseInt` truncation.

**Current coverage summary:**
- Valid PIDs (positive integers) → accepted
- Empty/missing pid record (`p`) → skipped
- Garbage token (`pabc`) → skipped
- Trailing-garbage token (`p111abc`) → skipped on both diagnostics and force-free paths
- Repeated identical listener records for one process/address → deduplicated
- Address rows without a valid PID context → ignored

target.title: fix(matrix): normalize message fields and deduplicate streaming m.replace events for CLI display
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Close #101420 Matrix `message read` and `message pins` CLI output renders completely empty tables — all four columns (Time, Author, Text, Id) are blank because the formatter doesn't recognize Matrix-native field names. Additionally, Matrix blocked streaming produces one `m.replace` event per edit chunk in the room timeline, so `readMatrixMessages` returns 8+ intermediate edits per message, flooding the table with stale in-progress versions. **Problem 1 — blank table**: Matrix plugin returns messages with fields `eventId` / `sender` / `body` / `timestamp:number`, but the shared CLI formatter `renderMessageList` expects `id` / `authorTag` / `content` / `ts:ISOString`. Zero field overlap → all rows blank. **Problem 2 — streaming noise**: Each `m.replace` edit chunk is a real event in the Matrix timeline. Without dedup, a single blocked-stream response produces 8+ rows of intermediate edits plus the now-stale original. ## Why This Change Was Made 1. **`tool-actions.ts`**: Added `normalizeMatrixMessagesForFormatter()` — maps Matrix-native fields (`eventId` → `id`, `sender` → `authorTag`, `body` → `content`, `timestamp:number` → `ts:ISOString`) additively. Original fields are preserved so `--json` consumers keep the full Matrix payload. `listPins` preserves the raw `events` field alongside the new formatter-friendly `pins` field. 2. **`summary.ts`**: `summarizeMatrixRawEvent` now prefers `m.new_content` over `content.body` for `m.replace` events — the outer `content.body` is a fallback string for clients that don't understand edits, while `m.new_content` carries the authoritative edit body per the Matrix spec. 3. **`messages.ts`**: Added `m.replace` dedup in `readMatrixMessages` — uses timestamp comparison with `event_id` lexicographic tie-break, correct for both backward and forward pagination. Filters out `m.replace` events that lack `m.new_content` (invalid per Matrix spec). Validates that the `m.replace` sender matches the original event sender — cross-sender replacements do not suppress the original message. Both changes are Matrix-plugin-internal. No shared formatter, other channel, or SDK contract changes. **Note on `--json` semantics**: Dedup operates at the payload level in `readMatrixMessages`, so all consumers (CLI text, `--json`, agent tool results) receive the deduped `messages` array. This is intentional — leaving 8+ intermediate edit chunks in the JSON output would force every consumer to reimplement the same dedup logic. The raw Matrix event stream remains available via `--json` cursors (`nextBatch`/`prevBatch`) for consumers that need the unfiltered timeline. ## Evidence - Matrix test suite: 123 files, 1433 tests, 0 failures - 10 new regression tests: backward/forward pagination dedup, equal-timestamp tie-break, cross-sender m.replace rejection, invalid m.replace filtering, non-replace message preservation, pins JSON/formatter output shape, m.new_content body priority, fallback when m.new_content absent - Live verification against a real Matrix homeserver: ``` $ node openclaw.mjs message read --target target.title: fix(openrouter): use dedicated /api/v1/images endpoint for image generation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's OpenRouter image generation currently goes through `/chat/completions`, treating image models as chat models and scraping images out of chat responses with ~300 lines of custom parsing. OpenRouter now ships a dedicated, OpenAI-compatible images endpoint (`POST /api/v1/images`), which is the supported path for image generation going forward and returns images in the standard `data[].b64_json` shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenRouter provider is rebuilt on the shared `createOpenAiCompatibleImageGenerationProvider()` factory — the same one used by xAI, DeepInfra, and LiteLLM — so it inherits the common auth, base-URL/config, timeout, SSRF, and response-size handling instead of maintaining a parallel implementation. Two small, backwards-compatible additions to shared code support this:

- A new optional `endpointPath` option on the factory, so a provider can target a flat path like `/api/v1/images` instead of the default `/images/generations` + `/images/edits` split. The path is appended to the resolved base URL; leading and duplicate slashes are normalized (both `"images"` and `"/images"` resolve to `<baseUrl>/images`), documented on the option and covered by factory tests (string, leading-slash, and per-mode function forms). Providers that don't set it behave exactly as before.
- The shared OpenAI-compatible response parser now reads `media_type` as a fallback when `mime_type` is absent (OpenRouter labels the image MIME type `media_type`). `mime_type` still wins when present, so other providers are unaffected.

The request body maps `model`, `prompt`, `n`, plus `aspect_ratio`/`resolution` for Gemini image models and `input_references` (data URLs) for image-to-image. The custom chat-completions parsing (`extractOpenRouterImagesFromResponse` and friends) is deleted.

The OpenRouter provider also enables the factory's magic-byte MIME sniffing: live testing showed the API omits `media_type` for PNG responses but can also return JPEG bytes without it, so sniffing keeps returned assets correctly labeled (an explicit `media_type` still takes precedence).

## User Impact

OpenRouter image generation and image editing keep working with the same configuration and models, now against OpenRouter's supported dedicated endpoint. Gemini image models gain aspect-ratio and resolution control, and multi-image references are passed through natively. No config changes are required.

## Evidence

### Tests

- `pnpm vitest run extensions/openrouter/image-generation-provider.test.ts` — 8 passed
- `pnpm vitest run src/image-generation/` — 53 passed (includes the shared factory tests, `endpointPath` normalization tests, and a `media_type` fallback test)
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/{xai,deepinfra,litellm,openai}/image-generation-provider.test.ts` — factory consumers unaffected, all passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` — clean (covers the `check-test-types` CI lane)
- oxlint + oxfmt clean on all changed files

### Live behavior proof (redacted)

Raw endpoint contract — `curl -X POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/images` with `{"model":"google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview","prompt":"a red bicycle leaning against a brick wall","n":1,"aspect_ratio":"1:1"}` (API key redacted). `HTTP 200`; response with `b64_json` elided:

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "usage": { "total_tokens": 1128 },
  "data": [
    {
      "media_type": "(absent — PNG default)",
      "b64_json_len": 3049104,
      "b64_json_prefix": "iVBORw0KGgoA"
    }
  ]
}
```

(`iVBORw0KGgo` is the base64 of the PNG magic bytes `89 50 4E 47`.)

End-to-end through this PR's provider code — a small driver script imports `buildOpenRouterImageGenerationProvider()` from this branch and calls `generateImage()` twice against the live API (text-to-image, then image-to-image feeding the first output back as a reference image):

```text
text-to-image  result: model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview mime=image/jpeg bytes=803555  magic=ffd8ffe0
image-to-image result: model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview mime=image/png  bytes=2020751 magic=89504e47
```

Both calls hit `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/images` (flat path, no `/images/generations` suffix), decoded to valid images (`file` reports `PNG image data, 1024 x 1024` / JPEG), and the reported `mime` matches the actual magic bytes — including the JPEG case where the API omitted `media_type`, which is what motivated enabling `sniffMimeType`.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): suppress unhandled rejections from void fire-and-forget calls
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem:** Four fire-and-forget `void` async calls in the WhatsApp extension could produce unhandled Promise rejections when their underlying asynchronous operations failed, which would crash the gateway.

**Solution:** Each call now uses `.catch()` to absorb the rejection. All four paths are best-effort: `logSelfId` is periodic status logging, and status reactions are non-critical lifecycle signaling.

**What changed:** +2 lines of `.catch()` handlers at four call sites in WhatsApp extension source; +3 test files with rejection-mocking regression tests; fixed 2 `check-test-types` type errors in the new test fixtures.

**What did NOT change:** No runtime behavior change for the happy path. No WhatsApp gateway startup logic, auth flow, or message processing pipeline changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Node terminates the process on unhandled rejections, so any of these failure modes could crash the gateway during normal operation:

- `logSelfId` called `loadWhatsAppChannelRuntime().then()` without catching dynamic-import failures
- `dispatchWhatsAppBufferedReply` called `statusReactionController.setThinking()` without catching network errors
- `dispatchWhatsAppBufferedReply` called `finalizeWhatsAppStatusReaction()` without catching state-transition errors
- `processMessage` called `statusReactionController.setQueued()` without catching rejection

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Two `check-test-types` CI failures: TS2345 (mock return type too narrow) and TS2352 (incomplete RuntimeEnv fixture). Both fixed in follow-up commit.

**Real environment tested:** Local Windows 10 x64 — openclaw git worktree at commit 0cb34bdcd7 with pnpm v11.2.2.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
# node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/channel.log-self-id.test.ts
# node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts
# node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-dispatch.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence:**

BEFORE FIX — CI reported 2 type errors:
```
TS2345: process-message.test.ts:602 — mock return type too narrow
TS2352: channel.log-self-id.test.ts:52 — RuntimeEnv missing exit
```

AFTER FIX — Local run confirming clean type-check:
```bash
# node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental
  ✅ PASSED
```

```bash
# node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental
  ✅ PASSED
```

All tests passing:
```bash
# pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/channel.log-self-id.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)

# pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts

      Tests  10 passed (10)

# pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/inbound-dispatch.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  54 passed (54)
```

**Observed result after the fix:** `check-test-types` now passes cleanly (previously 2 errors). All 65 WhatsApp extension tests pass. No unhandled rejections in test output.

**What was not tested:** Live WhatsApp gateway crash reproduction. The unhandled rejection paths are exercised at the unit-test level with mocked async failures. A live reproduction would require a WhatsApp gateway session with network conditions that trigger timeouts on status-reaction adapter calls — the mocked tests cover the same code paths (`statusReactionController.setQueued()`, `.setThinking()`, `loadWhatsAppChannelRuntime()`) with real rejection propagation through the `.catch()` handlers.

target.title: fix(status): surface auto-fallback model in status and session_status (#96126)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #96126. `openclaw status` and `session_status` now identify an active automatic model fallback without mistaking user-selected models, runtime snapshots, aliases, or configured subagent models for provider failover.

## What Problem This Solves

Status output showed the active model but did not explain when automatic provider fallback selected it instead of the configured primary. That made a provider outage look like an unexplained configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both status surfaces now carry a closed reason for a configured-versus-selected mismatch:

- user selection: pinned session, with the existing `/model default` recovery action;
- active automatic fallback: fallback selected, with provider-availability guidance;
- ordinary runtime snapshot, runtime-equivalent alias, or configured subagent self-origin selection: no warning.

The maintainer repair adds a shared active-fallback predicate at the session-provenance owner. A configured subagent intentionally stores automatic self-origin metadata so cleanup preserves its configured model; only an effective selection that differs from that recorded origin is provider failover.

## User Impact

- `openclaw status` labels real fallback rows as `auto fallback` and suggests checking provider availability.
- `session_status` shows the configured primary next to the live fallback model.
- User-pinned model wording remains unchanged.
- Configured subagent models remain normal configured selections, not fallback warnings.

## Evidence

- Sanitized AWS Crabbox `cbx_5b68069a77a2`, exact head `fd30f4666d7d80284d623073a5a1f59864a349e7`:
  - `run_921884422a68`: 39 focused tests passed across the provenance helper, CLI status summary/sections, and `session_status`.
  - `run_dde974d8aa34`: `pnpm check:changed` passed, including project type checks, lint/format guards, and dependency/import checks.
- Fresh pre-commit autoreview: no accepted or actionable findings.
- Focused regressions cover true automatic fallback, user pinning, runtime aliases, runtime-only snapshots, and configured-subagent self-origin state.

target.title: fix(infra): enforce maxBytes in readResponseBodySnippet non-streaming fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseBodySnippet` in `src/infra/http-error-body.ts` has a non-streaming fallback path that previously called `response.text()` which would buffer the entire body before `maxBytes` could be applied — creating an OOM risk for large error responses on non-streaming transports.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the whole-body fallback with a **fail-closed** approach: when the response body has no `getReader` (non-streaming or mocked responses), return `` immediately instead of calling `response.text()`. The streaming path continues to enforce `maxBytes` via the bounded reader loop.

This follows the ClawSweeper recommendation: *"use a bounded stream source or fail closed before calling whole-body fallbacks."*

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (8/8 PASS)

```
node --import tsx test/_proof_response_body_snippet_bound.mts

PASS  non-streaming fail-closed: returns empty string :: len=0
PASS  non-streaming small: also returns empty (fail-closed) :: got=""
PASS  streaming: snippet ≤ maxChars :: len=200 max=500
PASS  streaming: byte length ≤ maxBytes :: bytes=200 max=200
PASS  streaming small: passes through :: got="world"
PASS  streaming multibyte: bytes ≤ maxBytes :: bytes=15 max=15
PASS  streaming multibyte: chars ≤ maxChars :: chars=5 max=100
PASS  streaming multibyte: no replacement char :: snippet="啊啊啊啊啊"

[proof] 8 PASS, 0 FAIL
```

### Code change

The non-streaming fallback no longer calls `response.text()`:

```typescript
if (!body || typeof body.getReader !== "function") {
    // Fail closed: return empty rather than risk OOM on large bodies.
    return "";
}
```

Fixes #101269

target.title: fix(signal): retry debounce flush on reply session initialization conflict
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal's debounce flush handler silently drops inbound messages when the reply session initialization throws a "reply session initialization conflicted" error. Slack and Telegram handlers already handle this error, but Signal's `onFlush` handler has no retry mechanism, so follow-up DMs are permanently lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatch is wrapped with a bounded exponential backoff retry via the exported helper `dispatchWithRetryOnConflict`:

- Up to 3 retries (4 total attempts)
- Delays: 200ms → 400ms → 800ms (using `2 ** attempt`)
- Only retries on "reply session initialization conflicted" errors
- All other errors propagate to `onError` exactly as before

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (7/7 PASS)

```
node --import tsx test/_proof_signal_retry_conflict.mts

PASS  two conflicts then success: 3 total calls :: calls=3
PASS  always conflicts: error propagated :: err=Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:signal:direct:proof
PASS  always conflicts: 4 total calls (1 initial + 3 retries) :: calls=4
PASS  non-conflict error: propagated :: err=Error: some unrelated error
PASS  non-conflict error: only 1 call (no retry) :: calls=1
PASS  success on first attempt: only 1 call :: calls=1
PASS  custom params (2 retries, 50ms): 3 total calls :: calls=3

[proof] 7 PASS, 0 FAIL
```

## What Problem This Solves

`JsonRpcClient.start()` attaches `data` listeners to `this.proc.stdout` and `this.proc.stderr`, but does not attach `error` listeners. If either stream emits an `error` event, the unhandled error can crash the OpenClaw process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add no-op `error` handlers to both stdout and stderr streams:

```typescript
this.proc.stdout.on("error", () => {});
this.proc.stderr.on("error", () => {});
```

Stream read errors are treated as non-fatal because the process `error`/`close` handlers already report the real outcome.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(acp): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in printSessionUpdate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `printSessionUpdate` helper in `src/acp/client.ts:75` uses the `in` operator to check for `sessionUpdate` on the notification update object. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so it would match inherited properties — though unlikely in practice, `Object.hasOwn()` is the more correct semantic for own-property checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced `!(sessionUpdate in update)` with `!Object.hasOwn(update, sessionUpdate)` (1 line change). `Object.hasOwn()` (ES2022) is the standard own-property check, available since Node.js 16.9+.

## Evidence

The branch includes 3 regression tests in `src/acp/client.test.ts` that exercise the actual production code path against real `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` SessionNotification discriminator types:

2. **Non-sessionUpdate notifications** — correctly rejected
3. **Prototype-injected sessionUpdate** — rejected by `Object.hasOwn` but matched by `in` operator (demonstrates the fix prevents prototype pollution)

target.title: fix(macos): skip unresolved dashboard auth templates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101286.

macOS OpenClaw.app could treat `gateway.auth.token: "${OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN}"` as a literal local dashboard token when the GUI app environment did not contain that variable. That bypassed the LaunchAgent token fallback and produced a dashboard URL with an encoded placeholder fragment instead of a usable token.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Teach the local macOS auth resolver to recognize the same env SecretRef shorthand accepted by core config: `${NAME}` and `$NAME`, with `NAME` matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,127}$`.
- Resolve valid env SecretRefs from the app process environment when available.
- If a valid env SecretRef is unresolved, return nil so the existing LaunchAgent snapshot fallback can supply the local token/password, and so unresolved placeholders are never embedded in the dashboard URL.
- Keep non-matching strings such as `${custom_gateway_token}` as plaintext, matching the core SecretInput parser instead of introducing a broader Swift-only grammar.
- Keep remote gateway config token/password behavior unchanged.

## User Impact

Users launching OpenClaw.app from Finder/Dock can recover when the gateway token only exists in the per-user LaunchAgent environment. The dashboard URL uses the resolved LaunchAgent token when available, or omits token auto-auth instead of passing a raw placeholder. Existing literal strings that are not valid env SecretRefs continue to be treated as plaintext.

## Evidence

- Rebased the branch on current `origin/main` (`094c0d42`) and pushed head `7467386`.
- Contract checked against `src/config/types.secrets.ts`: `ENV_SECRET_TEMPLATE_RE`, `ENV_SECRET_SHORTHAND_RE`, and `ENV_SECRET_REF_ID_RE` accept only `${NAME}` / `$NAME` uppercase env ids.
- Docs checked in `docs/gateway/secrets.md`: public SecretRef docs list both `${OPENAI_API_KEY}` and `$OPENAI_API_KEY`, with id validation `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,127}$`.
- Added `GatewayEndpointStoreTests` coverage for `${NAME}` LaunchAgent fallback, `$NAME` LaunchAgent fallback, app-env template resolution, invalid lowercase template as plaintext, unresolved-template omission from the dashboard URL, and password fallback.

target.title: fix(file-transfer): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in dir-fetch tar operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from tar operations in dir-fetch (list, extract, unpack) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

`dir-fetch-tool.ts` spawns tar in three separate code paths with pipe stdio. All three consume stdout/stderr via `data` listeners and handle stdin EPIPE, but none register error listeners on the output streams. If the tar process terminates abnormally, Node emits `error` events on the unguarded stdout/stderr streams.

The fix adds no-op error listeners on every stdout and stderr stream across all three spawn calls, matching the established OpenClaw pattern.

## User Impact

Dir-fetch tar operations no longer risk unhandled stream errors during edge-case process terminations.

## Evidence

```text
$ git diff origin/main --stat
 extensions/file-transfer/src/tools/dir-fetch-tool.ts | 14 ++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 14 insertions(+)

$ npx oxlint extensions/file-transfer/src/tools/dir-fetch-tool.ts
  -> 0 errors

$ node -e '
  const ig = () => {};
  const s = new (require("stream").PassThrough)();
  s.on("error", ig);
  s.emit("error", new Error("EPIPE"));
  console.log("PASS: stream error suppressed");
'
PASS: stream error suppressed
```

- Each spawn already has `child.on("error", ...)` process-level and `child.stdin.on("error", ...)` stdin guards; the new handlers cover the remaining stdout/stderr streams.
- Third spawn uses `["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"]` -- only stderr needs the handler since stdout is ignored.

target.title: fix(file-transfer): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in tar listing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from tar listing in `dir.fetch` entry validation could silently swallow archive listing results instead of failing closed, weakening the archive validation security boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

`node-invoke-policy.ts` spawns `tar -tzf` with pipe stdio to list archive entries. The original fix used a no-op error listener, but ClawSweeper identified that this could let a partially-read archive pass final policy validation if stdout emits an error after only part of the listing was read.

The updated fix converts output stream errors into `ARCHIVE_ENTRIES_UNREADABLE`, killing the tar child, matching the existing fail-closed pattern already used for timeouts and oversized output in the same function.

## User Impact

`dir.fetch` archive entry validation no longer risks silently accepting incomplete tar listings when output stream errors occur. Stream failures are now treated as unreadable archives, consistent with all other error paths in the function.

## Evidence

```text
$ git diff origin/main --stat
 extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/node-invoke-policy.ts | 10 +++++++++-
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

$ npx oxlint extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/node-invoke-policy.ts
  -> 0 errors
```

- Each stream error now triggers `stopChild()` + `finish({ code: "ARCHIVE_ENTRIES_UNREADABLE", ... })`, matching the same finish signature used by timeout and oversized-output guards on lines 353-376.
- The existing `child.stdin.on("error", ...)` handler already uses `finish({ code: "ARCHIVE_ENTRIES_UNREADABLE", ... })` for stdin failures -- the new handlers extend the same fail-closed behavior to stdout and stderr.
